title: Steep
notes: MacBook Pro, Apple M2 Pro, 16 GB RAM, macOS 26.3.1. A short gameplay session worked well: the player reported "totally works super well" after the initial five-minute trial was extended. Exact active gameplay duration and FPS were not measured; 30 FPS is the configured cap. Long-session stability and online play remain untested. Launched the existing local steep.exe directly; Steam/Ubisoft installation and login flows were not validated. Without the DLL override, D3DMetal aborted during startup with: Call ... to unimplemented function D3D11.DLL.D3D11CoreCreateDevice, aborting The load trace showed d3d10core.dll and d3d10.dll loading immediately before the failure. The bundled DXMT d3d10core.dll imports D3D11CoreCreateDevice. Highball's D3DMetal overlay appends DXMT as a fallback in Sources/HighballKit/Bottle.swift. This suggests a mismatched D3D10 helper reaching D3DMetal's D3D11 library. Disabling d3d10,d3d10_1,d3d10core eliminated the observed abort and allowed the reported gameplay. Please treat this as a per-game workaround, not a global recommendation for D3D10 games. Other tested backends: DXMT rejected an 8-sample texture; this Mac's native Metal capability probe supported 1/2/4 samples, not 8. DXVK with d3d11.disableMsaa=True passed startup but the player reported oversized/stretched UI and severe host slowdown. D3DMetal plus the D3D10 override was the successful configuration. The successful D3DMetal trials used a timeout and memory watchdog. Timer-driven shutdowns were intentional, not reported game crashes. No game executable or original game DLL patches were made.
issues: No gameplay problems reported in the successful short session. The player selected 5/5 for the result after configuration. Setup required disabling D3D10 helpers to avoid a D3D11CoreCreateDevice startup abort; this is not an out-of-the-box compatibility claim.
